issues.where: signals(), lines 199-200: `if xi < m.n and xi > sg + 1: s.exit_short[xi - 1] = True` (and the docstring claim at lines 53-55)
issues.issue: When a target falls in a holiday gap, bar xi-1 closes before the target (targets 2018-12-25, 2019-01-01 and 2020-12-25). The marker on xi-1 then depends on the timestamp of bar xi. An adversarial truncation cut exactly at xi flags it: 3 of 5,549 cuts on AUDJPY and 6 of 6,112 on NZDJPY across all 12 cells. Only the exit_short field differs; entries and sl_dist never do, and the official leak report passes for all 12 cells on both markets. No price information is involved. The marker models a resting time exit filled at the first price after the target, which is what a live order gets and what the oracle modules do with exit[xi - 1]. The docstring sentence 'a truncated sample gives the same signals on its prefix' is not true in these few cases.
issues.fix: No change required. If strict prefix invariance is preferred, delete lines 199-200. The j0 marker (lines 206-207) and the fallback then give the same exit bar for every non-gap trade, and the 1-3 holiday-gap exits per cell move one bar later (for example 2019-01-01 22:00 to 23:00). In either case, add 'except the exit marker before a holiday gap' to the docstring sentence.

lookahead_risk: Low. Entries and stops use only closed-bar information. Each TFX row is used on the bar whose close is T*: ts_avail for Monday-Thursday rows, Monday 00:00 UTC for Friday rows, never before ts_avail. The price condition uses completed New York-close days and the ATR20 known at the start of the day. The de-overlap only looks forward from planned targets, and no statistic is computed over the whole sample. The official leak report passes for all 12 cells on AUDJPY and on NZDJPY. I ran 11,661 adversarial truncation cuts at every entry, fill, target and exit bar: 9 mismatched, all exit_short on the bar before an exit that falls in a Christmas or New Year gap (they depend on the next bar's timestamp, not its price). Perturbation in both directions at every third entry, fill and exit cut: 0 mismatches. One risk sits outside the code: ts_avail = date + 1 day 00:00 UTC (09:00 Tokyo) rests on the TFX report times (05:10 / 07:10 Tokyo, per the build script), and the entry fills at exactly that minute.
notes: Approve. No blockers; the four minor items are optional (1) or for the Director (2-4). I ran the module rather than only reading it. (1) An independent per-row implementation of the amended rules (R1, R2, item 9) gives the same entry bars, sl_dist and first exit marker as the module for all 12 cells on AUDJPY and NZDJPY. (2) AUDJPY design counts equal the R5 figures exactly: heavy10 100/76 at k 1.0 and 73/57 at k 1.5, heavy15 66/48 and 51/38, light 35/28 and 24/19. Check counts for heavy10 k 1.0 hold 2 match the projections: AUDJPY 37, NZDJPY 53, GBPJPY 18, USDJPY 0. NZDJPY design: heavy10 85/63 and 66/48, heavy15 52/38 and 46/34, light 50/41 and 26/21. (3) Every entry fills at the 00:00 UTC open of bar sig+1. Trades equal entries in all 60 market-cell runs, so no kept row is ever blocked by an open position. Time exits fall at the 20:00 UTC open on weekdays. The only exceptions are the reopens after holiday targets (22:00 on 2018-12-25 and 2019-01-01; the Sunday 2020-12-27 reopen for a Friday 2020-12-25 target in one NZDJPY light cell), as the 'holidays not skipped' rule intends. (4) 3,611 of 3,618 AUDJPY rows from 2010 to 2023 find a signal bar, and every one is date-aligned with D. The seven without one are year-end rows whose T* falls on 1 January. 722 of 723 Friday rows trade at the Monday open. Director's questions: (a) exit_utc 20:00 is correct for H1 bars. A 20:30 target means the 21:00 bar (the rollover hour), and on summer Fridays the Sunday open. PARAMS, the hypothesis.json params and the spec params all carry 20:00, but the rules and rationale texts are stale beyond the builder brief (issue 2). (b) All three departures are correct, and my code notes 3 ('sig < m.n - 1') and 6 ('keep the row only if xi < m.n') were wrong. An entry at sig may use bars 0..sig only, and both conditions make it depend on whether a later bar exists. I built a keep-rule variant in the scratchpad: it fails the official leak report in 2 of 12 AUDJPY cells (light k 1.0 hold 2 and light k 1.5 hold 4; entry_short and sl_dist mismatch at the 0.9 cut), as the Builder reported. Dropping the two conditions costs nothing: an entry on the last bar cannot fill, and a trade whose target lies past the end of the data closes at the last bar (none did in the pre-holdout runs). The added j0 marker is the same bar as xi - 1 everywhere except the holiday gaps, and it makes the normal-case exit causal (issue 1 covers the gaps). (c) The module runs on all five crosses. With spec.markets = [AUDJPY, NZDJPY], rule (4) must be restated before the run (issue 3), and the 40-trade minimum must be applied by hand (issue 4). Data: tfx_daily has one row per symbol per weekday; ts_avail = date + 1 day and oi > 0 on every row. The Large contracts (AUL/JPY and others) are not mapped to a symbol and are negligible (about 100 contracts, against 50,000-140,000 for AUD/JPY). Disclosure: while checking exit timing I saw the AUDJPY split of stop exits versus time exits. I computed no R, P&L or costs.
